title: Families 'devastated' as Stretford school closure announced

evidence_packet.title: Families 'devastated' as Stretford school closure announced
evidence_packet.lead: More than 50 pupils moved before the decision, while families fear losing local Catholic places
evidence_packet.summary: More than 50 pupils moved before the decision, while families fear losing local Catholic places
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Families 'devastated' as Stretford school closure announced - BBC News Image caption, Sue Green says she does not want to move her five-year-old daughter Bethany from St Teresa's before it closes next year By Haider Saleem Reporting from Greater Manchester Published 1 hour ago Families say they are devastated by a decision to close a Catholic primary school in Greater Manchester. St Teresa's RC Primary School in Firwsood, Trafford, will close down in August 2027. One mother told the BBC she feared she might not be able to get a place for her daughter at another local Catholic school. The council said falling pupil numbers had made the school's finances unsustainable. Council figures show more than 50 pupils secured places at other primary schools before the decision, leaving just 39 on its roll. Helen Fitzpatrick, 39, whose daughter Delilah attends St Teresa's, said families were "absolutely devastated" by the decision, announced on Monday. Fitzpatrick, who helped organise a campaign against the closure, said she had contacted nearby St Ann's RC Primary School but was told it could not guarantee Delilah a place for September 2027. Although a place was available when she enquired, she said she would have had to accept it immediately. "Delilah isn't ready to leave St Teresa's until it closes," she said. She said she feared Delilah could "get lost in the crowd" at a larger school. Delilah said she was "very sad" about the school closing. Image caption, Helen fears she may struggle to secure a place at another nearby Catholic school for her eight-year-old daughter Delilah Another parent, Sue Green, said she faced a similar dilemma over her five-year-old daughter Bethany. title: Plans for 17-storey tower by historic Marble Arch pub rejected

evidence_packet.title: Plans for 17-storey tower by historic Marble Arch pub rejected
evidence_packet.lead: The Grade II-listed Marble Arch has been serving pints on Manchester's Rochdale Road since 1888
evidence_packet.summary: The Grade II-listed Marble Arch has been serving pints on Manchester's Rochdale Road since 1888
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Plans for 17-storey tower by historic Marble Arch pub rejected - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, Plans for the 17-storey tower have prompted concerns over the Marble Arch's future By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago Plans for a 17-storey tower block next to a historic Manchester pub have been rejected by councillors. Developer The McGoff Group had applied to build 153 flats beside the Grade II-listed Marble Arch on Rochdale Road, which has been serving customers since 1888. The company said the scheme would deliver much-needed city centre housing and help regenerate the area. But the pub's owners argued the development threatened its future, and Manchester City Council's planning committee voted to refuse the application. In its objection, the pub said the 17-storey building would be "overbearing and oppressive" and would harm the setting of the pub. Councillors also raised concerns about the impact of the development on the Marble Arch and the lack of affordable housing in the scheme. Councillor Jon-Connor Lyons said he was "deeply concerned" about the effect on "one of Manchester's distinctive and much-loved historic pubs". A member of staff told the Local Democracy Reporting Service : "We get tourists coming from all over the world who are sent here. "We have generations of families drinking here, dads and grandads and sons. You don't get places like this anymore and it's something we want to keep going." evidence_packet.lead: Grace says the BBC Children in Need-funded holiday club helps her stay active and social
evidence_packet.summary: Grace says the BBC Children in Need-funded holiday club helps her stay active and social
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A teenage girl from Bramhall has thanked BBC Children in Need for helping to fund a school holiday club for students with learning difficulties The CADS (Children's Activities and Disabled Sports) programme is run by Stockport-based charity the Seashell Trust Grace Wilson, 14, with cerebral palsy, attends the sessions. She said: "I do bikes, drumming and swimming. Without it, I'd just chill around the house "I really love the staff because they're so bubbly and fun, like me" Grace's cerebral palsy means she struggles with her walking and suffers muscle pain in her legs She uses a wheelchair and has cochlear implants

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The family of an 86-year-old grandmother said her "agonising" wait in an emergency department rated by inspectors as one of the worst in England was an "absolute disgrace" Joan Jones was left "rolling over in pain" at the A&E department at Royal Albert Edward Infirmary in Wigan, Greater Manchester, her family said Her son, Barry Jones, said his mother had suffered a collapsed gallbladder and was in "constant pain" while waiting for treatment. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Doorman who witnessed racist outburst says abuse becoming normal - BBC News Image caption, Jawad Ali, 20, said he now expects racial abuse when he goes to work By Kaya Black North West Published 22 October 2026 A doorman who shared a video of a racist outburst he witnessed while at work has said such abuse towards staff is becoming "normalised". The footage, taken outside Ko-Ko Lounge in Rochdale, Greater Manchester, showed a woman shouting abuse and making gestures at a black security guard. Jawad Ali said the club-goer became abusive after being asked to move away from an exit while he was working at the venue on Saturday night. Greater Manchester Police said it had received a report about the incident and inquiries were ongoing. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, The video was shared widely on social media "It's disgusting," said Jawad, 20, who was working for Protective One Security at the time. He alleged the woman had also directed racial abuse towards him before the filming. Jawad said he decided to post the video on social media because "you can't do that and get away with it". "This isn't the first time, and it won't be the last," he added. Jawad said during the past two years working on the doors he has been called every racial slur and even threatened with death. "I expect now when I come to work to be racially abused one night out of the four that I work," he continued. "It's a normal thing now. It should be a big thing that gets prosecuted heavily." title: Women targeted by police officers who 'abused the badge'

evidence_packet.title: Women targeted by police officers who 'abused the badge'
evidence_packet.lead: Two women preyed upon by serving police officers describe their ordeals and why they are speaking out
evidence_packet.summary: Two women preyed upon by serving police officers describe their ordeals and why they are speaking out
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two women who were preyed upon by serving police officers they trusted have described their ordeals and why they decided to speak out Naomi Meadows was raped by a detective she met online in Devon, while Catherine Dobson was subjected to years of coercive and controlling behaviour by a Lancashire police officer who worked in a sexual offences unit Catherine said: "He used his job, he used his power and he abused the badge. Whatever his motives were, I will never understand." The women waived their right to anonymity to tell their harrowing stories as part of a BBC investigation that uncovered more than 1,200 domestic abuse allegations made in three years against police officers and special constables across England and Wales Professional standards investigations were opened into allegations including rape, sexual assault, grievous bodily harm, stalking and serious violence Most cases were discontinued, subjected to no further action or dropped because of a lack of evidence or victims withdrawing their complaints

evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Police said 46 properties were damaged across Greater Manchester since 5 October
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Police said 46 properties were damaged across Greater Manchester since 5 October
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Social media a factor in HMO attacks, says police boss - BBC News Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October By Naj Modak , North West and Ed Barnes , Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 22 October 2026 Social media is in part behind a spate of recent "racially or religiously motivated" attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) across Greater Manchester, a senior police officer has said. Greater Manchester Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October, including in Salford, Tameside and Stockport. Ch Sup Marcus Noden said footage of criminal damage was being shared widely "followed by comments and discussions", and people were using social media to "push the message out across different areas". He warned people to stop the attacks, which he said were "unlawful, reckless and putting lives at risk". As an investigation into the run of criminal damage continues, a 33-year-old man was arrested on Wednesday morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage and remained in custody for questioning. The damage was to HMOs or properties that were mistaken for HMOs. In Salford, 41 properties were targeted with three in Tameside and two in Stockport over the period. Image source, LDRS/MEN Image caption, Windows are seen boarded up on one property due to concerns of further attacks According to the Local Democracy Reporting Service , last week, two properties in Heaton Norris just outside Stockport town centre were targeted with anti-HMO graffiti. evidence_packet.title: M62 crash causes eight-mile queues and one-hour delays
evidence_packet.lead: Police say several vehicles were involved in the crash but no serious injuries were reported
evidence_packet.summary: Police say several vehicles were involved in the crash but no serious injuries were reported
evidence_packet.evidence_text: M62 crash causes eight-mile queues and one-hour delays - BBC News Image source, Highways England Image caption, National Highways reported delays of an hour and eight miles of congestion By Haider Saleem North West Published 22 October 2026 Drivers faced one-hour delays and eight-mile queues on the M62 following a crash during the morning rush hour. The collision happened on the eastbound carriageway between Junction 11 at Birchwood, near Warrington, and Junction 12 at the Eccles Interchange in Salford at about 06:35 BST. Greater Manchester Police said it appeared to involve several vehicles, but there had been no serious injuries or arrests - the road has since reopened. National Highways said one of the motorway's four lanes was closed for vehicle recovery at the time. Image source, Highways England Image caption, Long queues formed on the M62 eastbound following the early morning collision In an update at 08:38, the roads agency said drivers were facing delays of 60 minutes approaching the incident, with eight miles (13km) of congestion. Traffic camera images showed long queues of cars and lorries on the motorway. Police described the collision as involving vehicle damage only. title: Inquest hears of 'great danger' tip-off before fire murders

evidence_packet.title: Inquest hears of 'great danger' tip-off before fire murders
evidence_packet.lead: Social workers were told children were in "great danger" days before a fatal fire, an inquest hears
evidence_packet.summary: Social workers were told children were in "great danger" days before a fatal fire, an inquest hears
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in "great danger" days before they were murdered in an arson attack, an inquest heard Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is being heard at Bolton Coroners' Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told on 29 November, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: "The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Two women who were preyed upon by serving police officers they trusted have described their ordeals and why they decided to speak out Naomi Meadows was raped by a detective she met online in Devon, while Catherine Dobson was subjected to years of coercive and controlling behaviour by a Lancashire police officer who worked in a sexual offences unit Catherine said: "He used his job, he used his power and he abused the badge. Whatever his motives were, I will never understand." The women waived their right to anonymity to tell their harrowing stories as part of a BBC investigation that uncovered more than 1,200 domestic abuse allegations made in three years against police officers and special constables across England and Wales Professional standards investigations were opened into allegations including rape, sexual assault, grievous bodily harm, stalking and serious violence Most cases were discontinued, subjected to no further action or dropped because of a lack of evidence or victims withdrawing their complaints

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The passenger in a car driven by her cousin which dragged a head teacher more than a mile to his death denied "not telling the truth" to "protect" herself Gabrielle Debotte, 27, had told a jury that driver Simon Richardson knew 56-year-old cyclist Michael Mullins was under the wheels of his car after colliding with him at a junction on 20 April Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court has heard Richardson drove on for 1.36 miles (2.2km) until father-of-two Mr Mullins was finally thrown free on a country lane in Lymm, Cheshire, where he died a short time later Richardson, 35, denies he knew Mr Mullins was under the wheels and has pleaded not guilty to murder and an alternative count of manslaughter A jury has heard Mr Mullins, who was cycling to his home in Northwich from Stretford Grammar School, died from injuries the prosecution claim were caused by "dragging and crushing" rather than the impact of the collision itself On Wednesday Debotte said a short time after Richardson accelerated away from the crash site, on Paddock Lane in Warburton, Trafford, they heard the sounds of "moaning" coming from under the vehicle

evidence_packet.summary: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing
evidence_packet.evidence_text: This year marks 100 years since Wythenshawe Hall was donated to Manchester Corporation At the time, the city was in urgent need of more housing In 1920 an urban planner called Patrick Abercrombie identified Wythenshawe as the only undeveloped land suitable for building a housing estate close to Manchester To turn his proposal into a reality, Ernest and Shena Simon bought Wythenshawe Hall from Robert Henry Grenville Tatton in 1926, which they donated to the city's corporation (now known as the council) The idea was that people could be rehoused away from industrial Manchester into what became known as the "Garden City" To celebrate 100 years, BBC North West Tonight has spoken to 100 people from the area about what Wythenshawe means to them

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Social media is in part behind a spate of recent "racially or religiously motivated" attacks on houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) across Greater Manchester, a senior police officer has said Greater Manchester Police said there had been 46 properties damaged across the city region since 5 October, including in Salford, Tameside and Stockport Ch Sup Marcus Noden said footage of criminal damage was being shared widely "followed by comments and discussions", and people were using social media to "push the message out across different areas" He warned people to stop the attacks, which he said were "unlawful, reckless and putting lives at risk" As an investigation into the run of criminal damage continues, a 33-year-old man was arrested on Wednesday morning on suspicion of conspiracy to commit criminal damage and remained in custody for questioning The damage was to HMOs or properties that were mistaken for HMOs

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Drivers faced one-hour delays and eight-mile queues on the M62 following a crash during the morning rush hour The collision happened on the eastbound carriageway between Junction 11 at Birchwood, near Warrington, and Junction 12 at the Eccles Interchange in Salford at about 06:35 BST Greater Manchester Police said it appeared to involve several vehicles, but there had been no serious injuries or arrests - the road has since reopened National Highways said one of the motorway's four lanes was closed for vehicle recovery at the time In an update at 08:38, the roads agency said drivers were facing delays of 60 minutes approaching the incident, with eight miles (13km) of congestion Traffic camera images showed long queues of cars and lorries on the motorway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Social workers received an anonymous tip-off that children were in "great danger" days before they were murdered in an arson attack, an inquest heard Demi Pearson, 14, her brother, Brandon, eight, and sisters, Lacie, seven, and Lia, three, died after petrol bombs were thrown into their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, in the early hours of December 11, 2017 Their mother Michelle Pearson, 37, died almost two years later after suffering severe burns A joint inquest into their deaths, now in its third week, is being heard at Bolton Coroners' Court and on Wednesday it heard of social services involvement with the family The hearing was told on 29 November, 2017, less than two weeks before the fatal attack, the social services department at Salford City Council received an anonymous call The caller said: "The children are in a really unsafe environment and in great danger."

Simon Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane moments before the collision Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court On Thursday, jurors were told it was Mr Richardson’s case that he only realised Mr Mullins was underneath his car after he reversed his vehicle to return to the main road and his front seat passenger said there was “something” nearby

Their mother Michelle, 37, died almost two years later from the injuries she suffered in the inferno, Bolton Coroners' Court has heard The attack on their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, on December 11, 2017 was carried out by Zak Bolland, 26, and an accomplice amid a ‘tit-for-tat’ feud with Ms Pearson’s eldest son Kyle, 16 On Thursday (October 22) the joint inquest heard evidence from Kate Kennedy, who was principal officer with Salford housing provider Salix Homes at the time She told how Ms Pearson attended the provider on November 27, 2017, and presented as ‘homeless’. She spoke with a case officer and a form produced following the visit, she said, stated the reason Ms Pearson wanted to be moved from her home of 14 years was to ‘flee from violence’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Driver was 'unaware' Stretford Grammar headteacher was trapped under car after hitting him, trial hears Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:25, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Ima A driver was 'not aware' that Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins was trapped under his car until he was finally dislodged, a murder trial has heard. Simon Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane moments before the collision Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court On Thursday, jurors were told it was Mr Richardson’s case that he only realised Mr Mullins was underneath his car after he reversed his vehicle to return to the main road and his front seat passenger said there was “something” nearby

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Trafficked to the UK, beaten, raped and forced into sex work at dingy flats and houses - then they fought back Three men and a women involved in a Greater Manchester sex ring have been jailed for a total of 38 years View 5 Images (Top left) Ion Add to preferred sources News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 18:06, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 18:25, 22 Oct 2026 A man who ran a vile sex ring repeatedly beat and raped two women he forced to become sex workers at a network of brothels across Greater Manchester Ionut-Robert Marghiol, 37 was at the heart of an operation which brought Romanian women to the UK, where he put them to work as sex workers in Manchester, Bolton, and Bury Based in dingy flats and houses, the women were 'used as commodities' and were expected to have sex with different men for hours each day. The money they earned was taken from them and mostly kept by the gang Marghiol took their passports off them, and they were unable to leave or ‘live a free life’, a court heard. He ‘controlled’ them through the fear of violence, using them as ‘punchbags’ during almost daily beatings in which he also sometimes used weapons such as a baseball bat and He also repeatedly sexually attacked them during what a judge described as ‘in effect a campaign of rape’

title: Michelle Pearson had requested house move two weeks before deadly firebombing, inquest told

evidence_packet.title: Michelle Pearson had requested house move two weeks before deadly firebombing, inquest told
evidence_packet.lead: Salford Michelle Pearson had requested house move two weeks before deadly firebombing, inquest told An inquest into the deaths of Michelle Pearson and four of her children is ongoing Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:21, Housing bosses ruled against
evidence_packet.summary: Salford Michelle Pearson had requested house move two weeks before deadly firebombing, inquest told An inquest into the deaths of Michelle Pearson and four of her children is ongoing Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:21, Housing bosses ruled against
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Michelle Pearson had requested house move two weeks before deadly firebombing, inquest told An inquest into the deaths of Michelle Pearson and four of her children is ongoing Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:21, Housing bosses ruled against a request by the Pearson family for them to be rehomed two weeks before mum Michelle and four of her children were murdered in a petrol bomb attack on their home, an inquest has heard Demi, 15; Brandon, eight; Lacie, seven; and Lia, three, died after their house was firebombed. Their mother Michelle, 37, died almost two years later from the injuries she suffered in the inferno, Bolton Coroners' Court has heard The attack on their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, on December 11, 2017 was carried out by Zak Bolland, 26, and an accomplice amid a ‘tit-for-tat’ feud with Ms Pearson’s eldest son Kyle, 16 On Thursday (October 22) the joint inquest heard evidence from Kate Kennedy, who was principal officer with Salford housing provider Salix Homes at the time She told how Ms Pearson attended the provider on November 27, 2017, and presented as ‘homeless’. She spoke with a case officer and a form produced following the visit, she said, stated the reason Ms Pearson wanted to be moved from her home of 14 years was to ‘flee from violence’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bee Network Rail travel around Greater Manchester is about to change forever It is set to bring major beneftis from ticketing to infrastructure and the customer experience. Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 1 Rail travel around Greater Manchester is about to change forever with the first round of train stations set to join the Bee Network this December, with full integration across the region by 2030 The first 14 stations along the Glossop to Piccadilly line will join the network by the end of the year, with a further 15 from March 2027 including Stalybridge to Victoria and the Rose Hill, Marple and Hyde Loop lines Those stations will join Greater Manchester’s public transport network as part of the first phase of railway integration The second phase, by 2028, will see more key lines join the Bee Network with stations including Deansgate , Burnage, Stockport , Manchester Airport , Salford Central and Salford Crescent, Bolton , Rochdale , and Wigan Northwestern, among others The final phase of integration will be completed by 2030. The full roll out has been confirmed in a new Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) map published in a public report

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan The rules you need to follow in Wigan and Leigh or face £1,000 fine - full list Public spaces protection orders came in this week which include numerous bans including inappropriate e-bike use, public defecation and feeding the birds Add to pref New public spaces protection orders (PSPOs) have come into effect in both Wigan and Leigh town centres. evidence_packet.summary: Education 'Not the whole picture' blasts trust as two schools ranked worst for truancy in Greater Manchester Attendance and results have improved at both schools highlighted as England's worst for truancy Add to preferred sources Comments News Emma Gi An academy trust in charge o
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Education 'Not the whole picture' blasts trust as two schools ranked worst for truancy in Greater Manchester Attendance and results have improved at both schools highlighted as England's worst for truancy Add to preferred sources Comments News Emma Gi An academy trust in charge of two schools ranked among England's worst for truancy says they are undergoing 'rapid transformation' and absence figures don't show the full picture We reported earlier this week how Department for Education figures showed that Buile Hill Academy in Salford and Denton Community Academy in Tameside were in the top 20 schools for worst unauthorised absence rates Buile Hill was sixth on the list, with an absence rate of 11%, while Denton Community was 16th with a rate of 10.3%. A third Greater Manchester school - Dixons Brooklands Dixons Brooklands Academy in Wythenshawe - was in joint 20th position with a rate of 9.9% Both Buile Hill and Denton Community are run by the Northern Education Trust (NET), which took control amid 'significant challenges' relating to attendance, behaviour and exam results View 6 Images Buile Hill Academy (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

The Royton North councillor had led Oldham’s second largest party until he was replaced by Mark Wilkinson in September Mr Wilkinson then stood down as both leader of the group and Failsworth West councillor triggering a by-election. Reform Oldham is now led by Waterhead Coun Paul Taylor The Manchester Evening News can also reveal St James Coun Gary Tarbuck has also been suspended from the party. The two cases are understood to not be linked When approached for comment, a Reform UK spokesman said: “Coun Tarbuck was suspended from Reform UK pending investigation. Coun Quigg resigned from the Reform group mid-investigation.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Crime Gang used cruel cash machine trick to steal thousands from pensioners The three men would work together to distract their 'vulnerable' targets Add to preferred sources News Ashlie Blakey Live and breaking news reporter 13:49, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Three members of an organised crime gang have been jailed after they stole thousands of pounds from pensioners across the country using a cruel trick at cash machines Ionut Matei, 40, Vasile Ciubotaru, 45, and Ramonel Mandache, 51, together stole more than £40,000 from their 'vulnerable' victims. The trio targeted people using ATMs in Halifax bank, including in the Stockport and Bury branches, and at Lloyds Bank Detectives found Matei, Ciubotaru and Mandache, who are all Romanian nationals, would travel across the country during their malicious enterprise. To trick their victims, one of the men would stand close enough to see them entering their pin into the cash machine Another would distract them by drawing attention to a banknote deliberately placed on the floor nearby, Cheshire Police said. The third man would then swipe their bank card and replace it with a similar-looking card Victims were left completely unaware that their card had been stolen. The gang would then use the stolen cards and PIN to withdraw cash and buy items, often before the victims had realised what had happened

Known as 'Asda Roots', it will initially offer 16 young people permanent roles across eight stores, with plans to recruit Stores across the UK are involved in the scheme, including Asda locations across Yorkshire, Lancashire, Merseyside and the West Midlands. Across Greater Manchester, Asda's Longsight and Shaw , Oldham , supermarkets will also be hiring new apprentices The scheme is aimed at young adults, aged 18 to 21, who are not currently in employment, education or training, and the programme will combine permanent paid employment with structured on-the-job learning. Through the job, apprentices will work towards gaining a nationally recogn On the new scheme, James Goodman, Chief People Officer at Asda, said: "Too many young people are held back because they haven't had the opportunity to gain the skills and experience employers look for. evidence_packet.summary: Courts Driver was 'unaware' Stretford Grammar headteacher was trapped under car after hitting him, trial hears Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:25, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Ima A driver was 'not aware' tha
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Driver was 'unaware' Stretford Grammar headteacher was trapped under car after hitting him, trial hears Simon Richardson, 35, denies murdering Michael Mullins Add to preferred sources News Amy Walker Court reporter 18:25, 22 Oct 2026 View 4 Ima A driver was 'not aware' that Stretford Grammar headteacher Michael Mullins was trapped under his car until he was finally dislodged, a murder trial has heard. Simon Richardson, 35, is accused of hitting popular educator Michael Mullins as he cycled home from work on April 20 Prosecutors allege Mr Richardson did not stop and 'put his foot down', dragging 56-year-old Mr Mullins along the road for 2.2km - 1.3 miles - before leaving him to die on a grass verge on Wet Gate Lane in Lymm Jurors previously heard witnesses described seeing Mr Richardson's Volvo ‘absolutely tanking it’ towards the junction of Dunham Road and Warburton Lane moments before the collision Mr Richardson denies murder; an alternate offence of manslaughter; and dangerous driving. He is on trial at Manchester's Minshull Street Crown Court On Thursday, jurors were told it was Mr Richardson’s case that he only realised Mr Mullins was underneath his car after he reversed his vehicle to return to the main road and his front seat passenger said there was “something” nearby

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Trafficked to the UK, beaten, raped and forced into sex work at dingy flats and houses - then they fought back Three men and a women involved in a Greater Manchester sex ring have been jailed for a total of 38 years View 5 Images (Top left) Ion Add to preferred sources News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 18:06, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 18:25, 22 Oct 2026 A man who ran a vile sex ring repeatedly beat and raped two women he forced to become sex workers at a network of brothels across Greater Manchester Ionut-Robert Marghiol, 37 was at the heart of an operation which brought Romanian women to the UK, where he put them to work as sex workers in Manchester, Bolton, and Bury Based in dingy flats and houses, the women were 'used as commodities' and were expected to have sex with different men for hours each day. The money they earned was taken from them and mostly kept by the gang Marghiol took their passports off them, and they were unable to leave or ‘live a free life’, a court heard. He ‘controlled’ them through the fear of violence, using them as ‘punchbags’ during almost daily beatings in which he also sometimes used weapons such as a baseball bat and He also repeatedly sexually attacked them during what a judge described as ‘in effect a campaign of rape’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bee Network Rail travel around Greater Manchester is about to change forever It is set to bring major beneftis from ticketing to infrastructure and the customer experience. Add to preferred sources Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 1 Rail travel around Greater Manchester is about to change forever with the first round of train stations set to join the Bee Network this December, with full integration across the region by 2030 The first 14 stations along the Glossop to Piccadilly line will join the network by the end of the year, with a further 15 from March 2027 including Stalybridge to Victoria and the Rose Hill, Marple and Hyde Loop lines Those stations will join Greater Manchester’s public transport network as part of the first phase of railway integration The second phase, by 2028, will see more key lines join the Bee Network with stations including Deansgate , Burnage, Stockport , Manchester Airport , Salford Central and Salford Crescent, Bolton , Rochdale , and Wigan Northwestern, among others The final phase of integration will be completed by 2030. The full roll out has been confirmed in a new Transport for Greater Manchester (TfGM) map published in a public report

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Michelle Pearson had requested house move two weeks before deadly firebombing, inquest told An inquest into the deaths of Michelle Pearson and four of her children is ongoing Add to preferred sources News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 17:21, Housing bosses ruled against a request by the Pearson family for them to be rehomed two weeks before mum Michelle and four of her children were murdered in a petrol bomb attack on their home, an inquest has heard Demi, 15; Brandon, eight; Lacie, seven; and Lia, three, died after their house was firebombed. Their mother Michelle, 37, died almost two years later from the injuries she suffered in the inferno, Bolton Coroners' Court has heard The attack on their home on Jackson Street, Walkden, Salford, on December 11, 2017 was carried out by Zak Bolland, 26, and an accomplice amid a ‘tit-for-tat’ feud with Ms Pearson’s eldest son Kyle, 16 On Thursday (October 22) the joint inquest heard evidence from Kate Kennedy, who was principal officer with Salford housing provider Salix Homes at the time She told how Ms Pearson attended the provider on November 27, 2017, and presented as ‘homeless’. She spoke with a case officer and a form produced following the visit, she said, stated the reason Ms Pearson wanted to be moved from her home of 14 years was to ‘flee from violence’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Education 'Not the whole picture' blasts trust as two schools ranked worst for truancy in Greater Manchester Attendance and results have improved at both schools highlighted as England's worst for truancy Add to preferred sources Comments News Emma Gi An academy trust in charge of two schools ranked among England's worst for truancy says they are undergoing 'rapid transformation' and absence figures don't show the full picture We reported earlier this week how Department for Education figures showed that Buile Hill Academy in Salford and Denton Community Academy in Tameside were in the top 20 schools for worst unauthorised absence rates Buile Hill was sixth on the list, with an absence rate of 11%, while Denton Community was 16th with a rate of 10.3%. A third Greater Manchester school - Dixons Brooklands Dixons Brooklands Academy in Wythenshawe - was in joint 20th position with a rate of 9.9% Both Buile Hill and Denton Community are run by the Northern Education Trust (NET), which took control amid 'significant challenges' relating to attendance, behaviour and exam results View 6 Images Buile Hill Academy (Image: Kenny Brown | Manchester Evening News)

title: Former Oldham Reform leader resigns with immediate effect 'mid-investigation'

evidence_packet.title: Former Oldham Reform leader resigns with immediate effect 'mid-investigation'
evidence_packet.lead: Oldham Former Oldham Reform leader resigns with immediate effect 'mid-investigation' Another councillor has also been suspended pending investigation in what is understood to be an unrelated case Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Lo Former leader of Oldham Refo
evidence_packet.summary: Oldham Former Oldham Reform leader resigns with immediate effect 'mid-investigation' Another councillor has also been suspended pending investigation in what is understood to be an unrelated case Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Lo Former leader of Oldham Refo
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Former Oldham Reform leader resigns with immediate effect 'mid-investigation' Another councillor has also been suspended pending investigation in what is understood to be an unrelated case Add to preferred sources Comments News Edward Barnes Lo Former leader of Oldham Reform, councillor Lewis Quigg, has resigned mid-investigation while another elected member has been suspended, the party have said On October 22, Reform Oldham announced Coun Quigg had resigned from the party with immediate effect. The Royton North councillor had led Oldham’s second largest party until he was replaced by Mark Wilkinson in September Mr Wilkinson then stood down as both leader of the group and Failsworth West councillor triggering a by-election. Reform Oldham is now led by Waterhead Coun Paul Taylor The Manchester Evening News can also reveal St James Coun Gary Tarbuck has also been suspended from the party. The two cases are understood to not be linked When approached for comment, a Reform UK spokesman said: “Coun Tarbuck was suspended from Reform UK pending investigation. Coun Quigg resigned from the Reform group mid-investigation.”

Greater Manchester Police are concerned the evidence suggests a woman may have recently given birth Anyone with information, or who may have seen a woman in distress is asked to call police on 101 and quote incident number 684 of 22/10/2026 Detective Inspector Daniel Daly from GMP's Rochdale CID said: "Since receiving the report earlier today, we have been carrying out a number of lines of enquiry but our priority is to find the woman and make sure she is safe and well "She may be in need of urgent medical attention, and she is our absolute priority at the moment - that is why we are asking anyone with information to contact us." Shortly after 4.30pm, police confirmed that mother and baby had been found. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Salford Inside the glamorous Art Deco Salford home given listed status Broughton Park property is 91 years old Add to preferred sources Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 06:18, 22 Oct 2026 Updated 11:51, 22 Oct 2026 View 5 Images The 1935 hous A family home in Salford has been given Grade II listed status. The property on Old Hall Lane, Broughton Park, is described by experts as a "strikingly glamorous" house Built in 1935 it is a rare example of the international Streamline Moderne style that evolved from Art Deco. It features curved corners, long horizontal "speed lines," and a sleek, machine-age look inspired by ocean liners, airplanes, and trains Other examples of the style include East Finchley Tube Station in London and the Coca Cola building in Los Angeles. The design is characterised by flat roofs, horizontal emphasis, curved corners and dramatic glazing From the outside, this house is distinguished by slim brown brick facades, a flat roof, an exposed white concrete base, and windows that span both curved and angled corners View 5 Images A curved stair tower dominates the back of the house, while the entrance front steps back in stages, with an original single-storey garage reflecting the growing importance of the car in home design between the First and Second World Wars

evidence_packet.summary: The scheme would be delivered in partnership with Kerbo Charge
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The scheme would be delivered in partnership with Kerbo Charge Share on WhatsApp Share via Email Residents in Altrincham and across Trafford who don't have a driveway could soon be able to charge their electric cars at home using special channels installed in the pavement Trafford Council's Executive will consider proposals tonight for a one-year trial that would allow homeowners to install recessed charging cable channels across public footpaths, with the first 240 successful applicants receiving a £500 discount The scheme would be delivered in partnership with Kerbo Charge, whose system allows an electric vehicle charging cable to run through a narrow channel between a property and a parked car A flexible, self-closing lid sits flush with the pavement when the cable is removed, avoiding the trip hazards associated with cables trailing across footpaths The proposals could particularly benefit residents living in terraced properties and other homes without driveways

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Naomi Meadows was raped by a detective she met online in Devon, while Catherine Dobson was subjected to years of coercive and controlling behaviour by a Lancashire police officer who worked in a sexual offences unit Catherine said: "He used his job, he used his power and he abused the badge. Whatever his motives were, I will never understand." The women waived their right to anonymity to tell their harrowing stories as part of a BBC investigation that uncovered more than 1,200 domestic abuse allegations made in three years against police officers and special constables across England and Wales Professional standards investigations were opened into allegations including rape, sexual assault, grievous bodily harm, stalking and serious violence Most cases were discontinued, subjected to no further action or dropped because of a lack of evidence or victims withdrawing their complaints Campaigners say more needs to be done to tackle police-perpetrated abuse despite repeated warnings about failures to identify and remove dangerous officers in the wake of the 2021 murder of Sarah Everard in London by serving Metropolitan Police officer Wayne Couzens

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Gabrielle Debotte, 27, had told a jury that driver Simon Richardson knew 56-year-old cyclist Michael Mullins was under the wheels of his car after colliding with him at a junction on 20 April Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court has heard Richardson drove on for 1.36 miles (2.2km) until father-of-two Mr Mullins was finally thrown free on a country lane in Lymm, Cheshire, where he died a short time later Richardson, 35, denies he knew Mr Mullins was under the wheels and has pleaded not guilty to murder and an alternative count of manslaughter A jury has heard Mr Mullins, who was cycling to his home in Northwich from Stretford Grammar School, died from injuries the prosecution claim were caused by "dragging and crushing" rather than the impact of the collision itself On Wednesday Debotte said a short time after Richardson accelerated away from the crash site, on Paddock Lane in Warburton, Trafford, they heard the sounds of "moaning" coming from under the vehicle She told the jury her "panicking" cousin then wound his window down and said "he's under the car"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is introducing new orders to tackle anti-social behaviour in Wigan and Leigh town centres, including targeted powers against e-bikes and scooters These Public Space Protection Orders (PSPOs) will be in place for three years to support the police, council and other authorities in tackling a wide range of issues, reduce crime and help people feel safer in their communities This introduction follows an extensive review of previous orders and a public consultation held over the summer which gathered significant feedback from residents, businesses and the community sector Councillor Kevin Anderson, cabinet portfolio holder for Police, Crime and Civil Contingencies, said: “Residents, businesses and visitors all took part in our consultation, and it was clear that anti-social behaviour remains a concern “Most people who visit, live and work in our town centres do so responsibly, and these orders are aimed at addressing the small number of behaviours that negatively impact our communities, while ensuring support remains available for those who may be vulnerable.” The orders prohibit several anti-social behaviours, with new powers to enforce against anti-social use of cycles, e-bikes and scooters, and drug-related litter and paraphernalia

evidence_packet.evidence_text: We know residents have questions about the future of Gibfield and recent activity around the site. This update explains the current position, what survey activity means and how local people can take part in any future planning process In August 2026, Wigan Council’s Cabinet agreed to object to Peel Land’s proposed Gibfield Park masterplan. Cabinet’s position was that the housing and industrial proposals were not acceptable in their current form and did not have cabinet members’ support. No planning application West of Gibfield was allocated for homes, employment and green space through Places for Everyone, which was adopted in 2024 and now forms part of the statutory development plan. The current Wigan Local Plan process cannot reverse that allocation. However, allocation does not gran Our chief executive has written to the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, requesting Gibfield to be removed from the plan. We are waiting for a response Cabinet has formally objected to the proposed masterplan and made clear that it cannot support the development now or in the future Peel Land may undertake ecology surveys, ground-condition testing, environmental work and traffic or transport studies to understand the site and prepare evidence. These investigations do not mean planning permission has been granted or that a future application will be approved

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

Using sculpture, installation, film, photography In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. title: Beat the Jams Autumn season announced

event.event_name: Beat the Jams Autumn season announced

evidence_packet.title: Beat the Jams Autumn season announced
evidence_packet.lead: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians.
evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

evidence_packet.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. Please email learning@bandonthewall.org if you have any questions about this course

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Olllam is a band that fuses Irish traditional music with the modern jazz/post-rock energy of Detroit. Led by uilleann piper John McSherry, the band features Joe Dart (Vulfpeck), Michael Shimmin, Ross Ainslie, Seán O’Meara, and Joe Hettinga. Following their acclaimed album elllegy (RTÉ Radio 1 Best Group), The Olllam has collaborated with GRAMMY-nominated producer Zedd, shared the stage in Belfast with actor Anthony Boyle (Netflix’s House of Guinness), and recently completed a landmark U.S. tour in November 2025. From ancient airs to future soundscapes, The Olllam is not just carrying the tradition forward—they’re reinventing it

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The LGBTQ+ bar returns on Tariff Street with cocktails, food, live jazz, drag and late-night DJ sets By Manchester's Finest, Last updated 14 October 2026 Go to Manchester's Finest X profile LGBTQ+ cocktail bar Red Light will reopen in Manchester’s Northern Quarter on Friday 9 October, taking over a new space on Tariff Street The bar, founded by Deana Ferguson, will return next door to The Whisky Jar with a new look, an expanded food and drink menu and a programme of live music, DJs and performance The new Red Light features booth seating, a bar and club-style space, red lighting and an outdoor terrace, which will remain open until 11pm. evidence_packet.lead: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities.
evidence_packet.summary: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals

evidence_packet.lead: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, back
evidence_packet.summary: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, back
evidence_packet.evidence_text: It’s been a busy week at Labour Party Conference in Liverpool, with technology, growth and devolution featuring heavily in many of the conversations we’ve been part of In his first Conference speech as Prime Minister, Andy Burnham talked about devolving more power to places, backing businesses to grow and taking some of what has worked in Greater Manchester into a wider national approach. He also confirmed that AI will be a central focus of the That felt particularly relevant following an event we hosted through the UK Tech Cluster Group with AI Minister Kanishka Narayan, North East Mayor Kim McGuinness and other regional leaders, looking at AI, devolution and local growth One of the clearest themes from the discussion was that devolution should not mean every place trying to build the same thing. Different regions have different strengths, assets and specialisms, and there was a strong view that greater collaboration between places could create bi Procurement and buying local also featured strongly. The discussion highlighted the role public sector buying power can play in supporting regional businesses, helping successful pilots move into commercial contracts and strengthening UK capability in areas such as AI and cyber There was also a broader conversation about sovereignty and the UK’s role internationally. The discussion was not about trying to own every part of the AI stack, but about understanding where the UK already has genuine capability and where it makes sense to build more. Strengths

CEO Tom Keighley (pictured right) co-founded urfuture in Preston in 2024 with COO Jayel Williams (left) and CCO Holly Hobbs (centre). Innovation. Authenticity and three incredible individuals who don’t just understand the audience we’re trying to reach, they are that audience.” On Wednesday 28th October, he will speak on the breakfast panel at FUEL Manchester. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. Our Partner experts will be on Monex is a global financial services group with more than 40 years of experience helping businesses navigate global markets through foreign exchange expertise, market insights, and risk management solutions. Through its top-ranked research team, Monex is regularly recognised amon Representing Monex at this year's Forum will be Dr. Nick Rees , Head of Macro Research at Monex, alongside Katie Bragol i, Head of Corporate Sales, and Alex Kiddell, Executive from Monex UK During the event, Nick will explore the key geopolitical and macroeconomic themes shaping the global business environment as we look towards 2027. Drawing on insights from Monex's research team, he will discuss potential market implications arising from fiscal policy developments
